faq.q: Why can I hear distant trains better at night?
faq.a: At night the ground cools the air near it, leaving warmer air above. Sound bends back down from that warm layer instead of escaping upward, so faraway sounds reach you more clearly.
asks: Why is traffic louder at night?
Why does sound travel farther at night?

faq.a: Yes. Sound travels faster in warm air than in cool air. When sound passes through layers of different temperature, it changes direction, which is called refraction.
Normally air gets colder higher up. In an inversion, a layer of warmer air sits above cooler air near the ground. It often forms on clear, calm nights and over cold water.
asks: What does inversion mean in weather?
Why is it colder near the ground at night?

faq.q: Why does sound carry across a lake?
faq.a: Cold water cools the air just above it, making an inversion that bends sound back down. The flat water also reflects sound well, so voices carry a long way.
asks: Why can I hear people across a lake?
Why is sound clear over water?

faq.q: Why do sounds seem quieter on a hot afternoon?
faq.a: On hot days air near the ground is warmest, so sound bends upwards, away from the ground. Some sounds pass over your head and you hear them less.
asks: Why is it harder to hear far sounds on hot days?

facts: Sound travels faster in warm air than in cold air, about 0.6 metres per second faster for each degree Celsius.
Temperature inversions, with warmer air above cooler air, often form near the ground on clear, calm nights.
